flow: R12 failover preflight / durable quiescence request
authorityLaws: A2A CancelTask success is not by itself quiescence; the returned or subsequently fetched Task state must be interpreted.
A2A TaskNotCancelableError (-32002) is reconciled with GetTask because the task may already be terminal.
A2A TaskNotFoundError is not interpreted as quiescence because purging does not reveal whether the prior execution completed, failed, or was cancelled.
A2A TASK_STATE_COMPLETED routes to semantic verification rather than failover.
A2A protocol version is explicit per client/binding configuration and is never guessed from endpoint URL.
MCP tasks/cancel acknowledgement is not quiescence; R13 always follows it with tasks/get.
MCP completed routes to semantic verification; cancelled and failed prove execution quiescence but not replay safety.
MCP 2026-07-28 Tasks capability is attached per request and Mcp-Name is bound to taskId for task routing.
Remote non-loopback provider HTTP is rejected; HTTPS is required. Loopback HTTP remains available for local trusted integration.
Authentication headers are supplied by an out-of-band header provider and are not persisted in Agent Service semantic objects or rendered client reprs.
An empty effect list implies NO_EFFECTS only when the external effect-ledger snapshot explicitly declares complete coverage.
Incomplete effect coverage produces UNKNOWN, not safe replay.
PARTIAL or UNKNOWN effect state is not replay safe.
ROLLED_BACK and COMPENSATED classifications require explicit effect-ledger evidence.
A COMMITTED effect is replay safe only when the ledger provides a non-empty idempotency key bound to the exact fallback Binding.
Effect-ledger snapshot identity is bound to Task, source Binding and target Binding and mismatches fail closed.
R13 creates no effect database or shadow effect authority; it reads external evidence through EffectLedgerReader.
R13 does not change R12 durable quiescence/replay/claim-transfer authority and does not change R11 semantic completion authority.
Protocol idempotency and target-bound effect idempotency evidence do not become a universal exactly-once guarantee.

standardsBasis.use: CancelTask is idempotent but cancellation success is not guaranteed; GetTask is idempotent; clients explicitly send A2A-Version; terminal states include COMPLETED, FAILED, CANCELED and REJECTED.
Modern MCP is stateless; client capabilities ride each request; tasks/cancel is cooperative acknowledgement; tasks/get observes status; Streamable HTTP task requests bind Mcp-Name to taskId.
